title: Inference Detail
description: The local inference server in depth, whichever engine is resident (vLLM, SGLang or llama.cpp): throughput, load, latency, KV and prefix cache, request shape and outcomes, engine residency and limits.

list.name: host
list.label: Box
list.description: Inference box, by the host label vmagent stamps on every sample (listed if seen in the last 30 days).

list.name: model
list.label: Model
list.description: Models served in the last 30 days (vLLM / SGLang model_name). llama.cpp exposes no model label, so it only shows under All; Serving and Engine Residency ignore this filter.

panels.description: Which engine and model the inference server on the box is running right now, whatever the Model filter (llama.cpp exposes no model label). Offline = no engine metrics in the last 2 minutes.
Decode tokens per second, 1-minute rates over the last 3 hours (any engine). 'not serving' = no engine (for the selected model) reporting.
Requests being processed, peak per minute over the last 3 hours.
Requests waiting for a slot, peak per minute. Anything above 0 means the engine is at capacity (amber).

Share of the KV cache in use (vLLM kv_cache_usage_perc / SGLang token_usage), peak per minute. Amber from 90%, red from 98% -- a full cache preempts requests. '–' when no engine reports it (offline, or llama.cpp).
95th-percentile time to first token over the last hour, per engine histogram (vLLM / SGLang; llama.cpp exports none). 'no data' when nothing finished in the hour or llama.cpp is resident.

Requests finished since local midnight (vLLM / SGLang request counters; llama.cpp exposes none, so its traffic is not counted): a running sum of 5-minute increases, each window one step ahead so the day starts at midnight and the last step reaches now.

panels.title: Generation
panels.description: Decode (generation) tokens per second across whichever engine is resident. $__rate_interval widens with the step so long ranges average instead of aliasing.

panels.title: Prefill
panels.description: Prompt tokens per second, stacked: computed by the engine (real prefill work) and served from the prefix cache. The engines count differently -- vLLM and SGLang prompt totals include cache hits, llama.cpp's do not -- so each side is taken from its own counter (vLLM prompt_tokens_by_source local_compute / local_cache_hit, SGLang uncached / cached tokens, llama.cpp prompt / prompt_cached tokens). Counting cache hits as prefill overstated vLLM prefill about 5.7x.

panels.title: Concurrency
panels.description: Requests running and queued, peak per step. A queue that stays above zero means the engine is at capacity.

panels.title: Time to First Token
panels.description: p50 (solid) and p95 (dashed) time to first token, per engine histogram. Gaps: no request finished in that step, or llama.cpp was resident (it exports no latency histograms; its mean time per generated token is drawn in Inter-token Latency).

panels.title: Inter-token Latency
panels.description: p50 and p95 gap between generated tokens for one request -- 1 / this is the per-stream decode speed (17.5 ms is about 57 tok/s). llama.cpp has no histogram: its mean time per generated token (dotted) comes from tokens_predicted_seconds / tokens_predicted. Gaps: no request finished in that step, or llama.cpp was resident (it exports no latency histograms; its mean time per generated token is drawn in Inter-token Latency).

panels.title: End-to-end Latency
panels.description: p50 and p95 total request time, first byte in to last token out. Gaps: no request finished in that step, or llama.cpp was resident (it exports no latency histograms; its mean time per generated token is drawn in Inter-token Latency).

panels.title: Queue Time
panels.description: p50 and p95 time requests waited before being scheduled -- rises when the KV cache or batch is full. Gaps: no request finished in that step, or llama.cpp was resident (it exports no latency histograms; its mean time per generated token is drawn in Inter-token Latency).

panels.title: KV Cache
panels.description: Share of the KV cache in use, peak per step (vLLM kv_cache_usage_perc / SGLang token_usage). Near 100% the engine starts preempting requests (see Preemptions in Engine Limits).

panels.title: Prefix Cache Hits
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens served from the prefix cache in each step: vLLM prefix_cache_hits / queries, SGLang cached / prompt tokens, llama.cpp prompt_tokens_cached / (prompt + cached) -- llama.cpp's prompt counter excludes cache hits, so dividing by it alone read 330-3,250%. With long agentic prompts this is what keeps prefill cheap. Gaps mean no prompts in that step.

panels.title: Request Shape
panels.description: Tokens per request: prompt (magenta) and generated (blue), p50 solid and p95 dashed, on a log axis -- prompts here are two orders of magnitude longer than completions. Per-engine histograms (vLLM / SGLang; llama.cpp has none).

panels.title: Request Outcomes
panels.description: How requests ended, per step: completed normally, cut off at max tokens, aborted (client disconnect / cancel), or errored. vLLM reports finished_reason; SGLang's finished-request count includes aborts, so completed = finished - aborted. llama.cpp exports no request counters. Normal completions stay grey so problems stand out.

panels.title: Engine Residency
panels.description: Which engine and model the box was serving over the range, one row each (a gap = nothing serving / box off). Ignores the Model filter.

panels.title: Engine Limits
panels.description: Capacity of the resident engine, evaluated now: KV-cache capacity in tokens (vLLM cache_config_info / SGLang max_total_num_tokens), full-context requests that fit at once (vLLM kv_cache_max_concurrency), context window (SGLang context_len / llama.cpp n_tokens_max), GPU memory share the engine claimed (vLLM gpu_memory_utilization), requests preempted over the range (vLLM), and speculative-decoding acceptance (SGLang spec_accept_rate / llama.cpp accepted / drafted). '–' = not exposed by the resident engine.
